elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Upon written notice from Client to TrueLink, the license granted under section 2(a) extends to the affiliates of Client identified in that notice", and § 8(c) is conformed to permit access by "its and its licensed affiliates' officers, employees, and agents".

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant in § 2(a) and the new Affiliates and Successors clause run only to Client and identified affiliates; no operative language extends the licence to contractors acting on Client's behalf. § 8(c) merely restricts access (including "agents"), which is an access limitation, not a licence extension.

The cited text contains no fee/paid-up mechanic; § 2(c) provides only that "The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12", and no perpetual paid-up licence language was added. Whether any paid-up licence exists cannot be determined from the supplied paragraphs.
No irrevocability language appears anywhere in the rendered text, and the supplied paragraphs do not establish whether a paid-up licence category exists under this term-limited grant.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: § 2(c) is retained unchanged and ties licence duration to termination "in accordance with section 12"; no limitation confining licence termination to uncured material breach was added, and § 12's grounds are untouched.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Client may transfer the license to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction without TrueLink's approval" — a Client-only right, not a widening of the mutual § 15 exception.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "Upon written notice from Client to TrueLink, the license granted under section 2(a) extends to the affiliates of Client identified in that notice"; the § 8(c) access restriction is conformed so licensed affiliates' personnel may access the Interface, so the coverage is operative rather than nominal.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "Client may transfer the license to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction without TrueLink's approval" — express, unconditional, Client-side, and expressly free of Vendor consent.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both fallback elements are met by the inserted "Affiliates and Successors" clause in § 2, and the conforming edit to § 8(c) is necessary so the affiliate licence is not defeated by the retained access restriction limiting Interface access to Client's own officers, employees and agents.

Preferred level is not complete. To reach it the drafter would need to (i) add "and contractors acting on Client's behalf" to the § 2(a) grant, (ii) add perpetual and irrevocable status for any fully paid-up licence, and (iii) amend § 2(c) so the licence terminates only on Client's uncured material breach rather than on any termination under § 12.

Minimality holds: the only changes are the concise § 2 insertion and the narrow § 8(c) conforming words; § 2(a), § 2(c), § 2(d) and § 15 are otherwise retained verbatim, including the Customer-favourable non-exclusivity/free-to-use-alternatives sentence, and no survival, expense, remedy or procedural extras were added.

Intent is preserved: the successor right is implemented as a Client-only transfer power in § 2 rather than as a new mutual assignment exception in § 15, so Vendor gains no new assignment freedom. Drafting nits worth tightening but not defeating the position: the inserted clause is unlettered (should be § 2(e)) and would read more cleanly as "Notwithstanding Section 15, ..." to foreclose any argument that § 15's general prior-approval requirement still bites on the M&A transfer; consider also defining "licensed affiliates" by cross-reference to the new clause.
